papers.title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain. Results Utilizing questions from Rosalind, a bioinformatics educational platform, we compare the performance of the LLMs on 104 questions relative to expert ground truth and 68,760 humans with varying levels of expertise. Among the frontier LLMs evaluated (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Llama-4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5.2 exhibited top performance, providing correct answers for 80/104 (77%) questions followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6. LLM performance varied widely depending on the biological categories of questions. While the latest generation of frontier LLM models showed overall improvements in performance, their performance in specific categories of biological questions was lower than first generation models. Overall, LLMs performance mirrored that of humans with lower performance in tasks in which humans had low performance and vice versa. However, LLMs also failed in some instances where most humans were correct and, in a few cases, LLMs excelled where most humans failed. To the best of our knowledge, this presents the first assessment of general purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks in distinct areas relative to both expert and non-expert ground truths. Availability and Implementation The complete analysis was implemented in Python; all code is available at https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics

papers.llm_title_zh: 评估大型语言模型在那些需要多步骤推理与代码编写的基本生物信息学任务中的表现

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：大型语言模型、人工智能代理以及各类辅助工具有望加速从化学到生物学等各个领域的科学研究进展。
llm_highlights_zh: 生物信息学——对DNA、RNA及蛋白质序列的分析在生物学研究中发挥着至关重要的作用，由于其本质上属于计算科学领域，因此特别适合通过人工智能技术实现自动化处理。
在这里，我们通过一系列涵盖基础分析任务的测试，评估了当前流行的通用大型语言模型的生物信息学处理能力。这些任务包括代码编写以及该领域中的多步骤推理过程。
结果：我们利用生物信息学教育平台Rosalind上的问题，对比了这些大型语言模型在104道题目上的表现。这些题目的参考答案由专家提供，同时我们也统计了68,760名具有不同专业水平的人在这些题目上的答题情况。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
大型语言模型、人工智能工具以及人类科学家共同为加速从化学到生物学等各个领域的科学研究带来了巨大潜力。生物信息学——即对DNA、RNA和蛋白质序列的分析——在生物学研究中发挥着至关重要的作用，由于其计算性质，这一领域特别适合通过人工智能技术实现自动化处理。本研究评估了当前流行的通用大型语言模型在一系列基础生物信息学任务中的表现，这些任务涵盖了代码编写及多步骤推理等关键环节。  

**研究结果**  
我们利用生物信息学教育平台Rosalind提供的测试题目，对比了这些大型语言模型在104道题目上的表现，并将这些结果与专家给出的正确答案以及68,760名具有不同专业水平的人类用户的答题结果进行了对照分析。在所评估的先进大型语言模型中（GPT-5.2、GPT-4o、GPT-3.5、Llama-3-70B、Llama-4及Claude Sonnet 4.6），GPT-5.2的表现最为突出，它在104道题目中的80道（占77%）上给出了正确答案，其次是Claude Sonnet 4.6。不同类型的生物信息学问题对大型语言模型的表现影响显著：尽管最新一代的大型语言模型在整体性能上有所提升，但它们在某些特定领域的表现仍低于第一代模型。总体而言，这些模型的表现与人类的水平相当——在人类表现较差的领域中，模型也会表现出较低的水平；反之亦然。不过，在一些问题上，大多数人类用户都能做出正确答案，而大型语言模型却会出错；而在另一些情况下，大型语言模型反而能取得比人类更好的成绩。据我们所知，这是首次针对不同生物信息学领域的基础任务，同时结合专家与非专家的标准答案来评估通用大型语言模型的表现。  

**实现方式与代码公开**  
整个分析过程是用Python编写的，所有相关代码均可在以下链接获取：https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics

all_papers.title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain. Results Utilizing questions from Rosalind, a bioinformatics educational platform, we compare the performance of the LLMs on 104 questions relative to expert ground truth and 68,760 humans with varying levels of expertise. Among the frontier LLMs evaluated (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Llama-4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5.2 exhibited top performance, providing correct answers for 80/104 (77%) questions followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6. LLM performance varied widely depending on the biological categories of questions. While the latest generation of frontier LLM models showed overall improvements in performance, their performance in specific categories of biological questions was lower than first generation models. Overall, LLMs performance mirrored that of humans with lower performance in tasks in which humans had low performance and vice versa. However, LLMs also failed in some instances where most humans were correct and, in a few cases, LLMs excelled where most humans failed. To the best of our knowledge, this presents the first assessment of general purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks in distinct areas relative to both expert and non-expert ground truths. Availability and Implementation The complete analysis was implemented in Python; all code is available at https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics

Among the frontier LLMs evaluated (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Llama-4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5.2 exhibited top performance, providing correct answers for 80/104 (77%) questions followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6. While the latest generation of frontier LLM models showed overall improvements in performance, their performance in specific categories of biological questions was lower than first generation models. Overall, LLMs performance mirrored that of humans with lower performance in tasks in which humans had low performance and vice versa. However, LLMs also failed in some instances where most humans were correct and, in a few cases, LLMs excelled where most humans failed. To the best of our knowledge, this presents the first assessment of general purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks in distinct areas relative to both expert and non-expert ground truths.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The complete analysis was implemented in Python; all code is available at https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics.

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
大型语言模型、人工智能工具以及人类科学家共同为加速从化学到生物学等各个领域的科学研究带来了巨大潜力。生物信息学——即对DNA、RNA和蛋白质序列的分析——在生物学研究中发挥着至关重要的作用，由于其计算性质，这一领域特别适合通过人工智能技术实现自动化处理。本研究评估了当前流行的通用大型语言模型在一系列基础生物信息学任务中的表现，这些任务涵盖了代码编写及多步骤推理等关键环节。  

**研究结果**  
我们利用生物信息学教育平台Rosalind提供的测试题目，对比了这些大型语言模型在104道题目上的表现，并将这些结果与专家给出的正确答案以及68,760名具有不同专业水平的人类用户的答题结果进行了对照分析。在所评估的先进大型语言模型中（GPT-5.2、GPT-4o、GPT-3.5、Llama-3-70B、Llama-4及Claude Sonnet 4.6），GPT-5.2的表现最为突出，它在104道题目中的80道（占77%）上给出了正确答案，其次是Claude Sonnet 4.6。不同类型的生物信息学问题对大型语言模型的表现影响显著：尽管最新一代的大型语言模型在整体性能上有所提升，但它们在某些特定领域的表现仍低于第一代模型。总体而言，这些模型的表现与人类的水平相当——在人类表现较差的领域中，模型也会表现出较低的水平；反之亦然。不过，在一些问题上，大多数人类用户都能做出正确答案，而大型语言模型却会出错；而在另一些情况下，大型语言模型反而能取得比人类更好的成绩。据我们所知，这是首次针对不同生物信息学领域的基础任务，同时结合专家与非专家的标准答案来评估通用大型语言模型的表现。  

**实现方式与代码公开**  
整个分析过程是用Python编写的，所有相关代码均可在以下链接获取：https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain.

RESULTS: Utilizing questions from Rosalind, a bioinformatics educational platform, we compare the performance of the LLMs on 104 questions relative to expert ground truth and 68,760 humans with varying levels of expertise. Among the frontier LLMs evaluated (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Llama-4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5.2 exhibited top performance, providing correct answers for 80/104 (77%) questions followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6. LLM performance varied widely depending on the biological categories of questions. While the latest generation of frontier LLM models showed overall improvements in performance, their performance in specific categories of biological questions was lower than first generation models. Overall, LLMs performance mirrored that of humans with lower performance in tasks in which humans had low performance and vice versa. However, LLMs also failed in some instances where most humans were correct and, in a few cases, LLMs excelled where most humans failed. To the best of our knowledge, this presents the first assessment of general purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks in distinct areas relative to both expert and non-expert ground truths.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The complete analysis was implemented in Python; all code is available at https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
